page: Google Cloud Platform m4-megamem-224 is an ultra-high-memory server instance built on the x86_64 architecture. The system provides 224 dedicated vCPUs along with 2976 GB of system memory. This resource configuration yields approximately 13.29 GB of RAM per vCPU, placing it firmly in the memory-optimized classification for hyper-scale processing requirements.

Hardware allocation on this instance omits integrated local storage and GPU accelerators, leaving local storage at none and GPU count at zero. As a result, disk input and output operations rely entirely on remote network block storage. No complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default, requiring separate network configuration for external addressing.

Standard benchmark metrics are not provided in the data for this profile. However, cost efficiency is dictated by the density of dedicated compute and massive memory allocation. The server provides economic value primarily when application architectures fully utilize the near-three-terabyte memory footprint. Typical deployment targets include large in-memory databases, massive transactional datastores, complex in-memory analytics engines, and enterprise resource planning systems.
description: Google Cloud Platform m4-megamem-224 is a memory-optimized server configuration designed for large-scale enterprise applications requiring extensive RAM capacity. Powered by the x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 224 dedicated virtual CPUs paired with 2976 GB of system memory, delivering a high memory density of 13.29 GB per core. The instance operates without discrete GPU acceleration and includes no onboard local storage, necessitating external network-attached block volumes for operating systems and data retention. While standardized benchmark measurements are not recorded for this tier, the system is architected to balance high multi-core throughput with substantial physical memory allocation. Due to its concentrated hardware footprint, cost efficiency centers on maximizing utilization of the large memory pool. The configuration is primarily matched to memory-bound enterprise deployments, including large in-memory databases, enterprise resource planning systems, high-volume transactional data stores, and real-time data analytics pipelines.
